label: Year-end bonus (PC 200)
answer: Yes, part-timers are entitled to it. Under PC 200 it's pro rata to their working regime and the months worked in the reference year, provided they have at least 6 months of seniority. I did exactly this calculation two weeks ago, happy to share the template.

label: Salary indexation (PC 200)
answer: PC 200 indexes once a year, on 1 January, based on the index evolution of the previous year. It applies to actual salaries, not just the minimum scales. Fixed allowances only follow if the contract or policy says so.

label: Part-time employment
answer: A part-time schedule has to be in writing and included in the work regulations. Most benefits follow pro rata. Watch the minimum of one third of a full-time schedule and at least 3 hours per work period.

label: Notice period (Netherlands)
answer: For the employer it's 1 month under 5 years of service, 2 months for 5-10 years, 3 for 10-15 and 4 months beyond 15 years. The employee gives 1 month. Always check the collective agreement (cao) first, it can deviate.

label: Notice period (Belgium)
answer: Since the unified status it's calculated in weeks based on seniority. Seniority from before 2014 is calculated separately under the old rules and added up. Send me the start date and I'll run it through our calculator.

label: Company car & benefit in kind
answer: The benefit in kind depends on the catalogue value, the CO2 emission and the car's age, with a yearly minimum amount. An own contribution by the employee can be deducted from it. For hybrids, check the date the car was ordered.

label: Meal & eco vouchers
answer: Meal vouchers are granted per day actually worked, so sick days don't count. Eco vouchers are pro rata for part-timers and new hires, based on the reference period in the sector agreement.

label: Telework & home office allowance
answer: A structural teleworker can receive a tax-free home office allowance up to the yearly indexed ceiling, on top of a lump sum for internet and screen. It needs a written telework agreement.

label: Cross-border workers (Luxembourg)
answer: The number of days a Luxembourg worker can work from Belgium without tax consequences has changed since I last worked on this. Please double-check with the tax team before answering the client.

label: German payroll & social security
answer: Register the entity with the Betriebsnummer first, then each employee with the social security funds. Tax classes can change mid-year; the new class applies from the next payroll.

label: French payroll (DSN)
answer: The DSN is filed monthly, and a rejection usually comes from a mismatch in the contract or establishment identifiers. Fix the block and resubmit within the same month to avoid penalties.

label: GDPR & employee data retention
answer: Payroll records have legal retention periods of several years, so they can't be deleted on request. For an access request you have one month to reply, and you share only that person's data.

label: Sick leave & guaranteed salary
answer: A relapse within 14 days of returning to work counts as the same illness, so no new guaranteed salary period starts. Check the sector rules for when the medical certificate must be received.

label: Parental & birth leave
answer: Birth leave for the co-parent has to be taken within 4 months after the birth. Parental leave can be taken full-time, half-time, 1/5 or 1/10 (the latter with employer approval).

label: Holiday pay
answer: White-collar workers get double holiday pay from the employer, usually in May or June. When someone leaves, the leaving certificate settles it and the next employer deducts what was already paid.

label: Overtime
answer: Voluntary overtime has a yearly limit of hours and doesn't have to be recovered, but it still gets the overtime premium. Regular overtime needs recovery rest unless the employee chooses payment.

label: Flexi-jobs
answer: The person needs at least a 4/5 job with another employer in the reference quarter, or be retired. The flexi-wage has a minimum and the employer pays a special contribution.

label: Student workers
answer: Students can work 475 hours per year at the reduced solidarity contribution. Check their remaining counter on Student@work before every contract, and file a Dimona STU.

label: Monthly payroll close & payslip corrections
answer: After the close we don't reopen the run. Corrections go into the next payroll as a regularisation, unless the net difference is urgent; then we do an off-cycle payment.

label: Expat taxation
answer: The Belgian inbound taxpayer regime has to be requested within 3 months of starting. There's a minimum salary condition, except for researchers, and tax-free cost allowances are capped.

label: Group insurance & supplementary pension
answer: New hires join the plan from their first day. Part-timers can't be excluded, and contributions on variable pay depend on the plan rules, so check the definition of salary in the regulations.

label: Cafeteria plan & flexible reward
answer: The budget has to come from a new or variable element, not the fixed salary. Each option keeps its own tax treatment, so a bike lease in the plan stays favourable but cash-out is taxed as salary.

label: Dimona & new-hire onboarding
answer: Dimona IN must be filed at the latest when the employee starts working. If the start date changes, update the Dimona before that date, not after.

label: Time credit & career break
answer: Time credit with a motive (like caring for a child) can be taken full-time, half-time or 1/5. The employee applies in writing with enough notice, and the employer can postpone it in some cases.

label: Mobility budget
answer: Only employees who have or could have a company car are eligible. The budget has three pillars: an eco-friendly car, sustainable mobility (bike, public transport, housing costs) and cash for the rest, which is taxed.

label: Bike allowance & bike lease
answer: The bike allowance is tax-free per kilometre up to a yearly cap, also for speed pedelecs. A leased bike is fine to combine with the allowance, and private use of the lease bike isn't taxed as a benefit.

label: EV home charging reimbursement
answer: We reimburse home charging at the official kWh price set by the government each quarter, based on the car's charging logs. The charging station at home can be paid by the employer without it becoming a benefit if it's part of the car policy.

label: Working remotely from abroad
answer: Short stays are usually fine, but you need an A1 certificate for social security, and after a certain number of days tax and permanent establishment risks start. Our policy allows up to 20 days per year without approval.

label: Temporary unemployment
answer: For economic reasons the employer has to notify the employees and the national employment office in advance, with the days planned. The employees get an unemployment benefit plus an employer supplement defined by the sector.

label: Holiday entitlement (Netherlands)
answer: Statutory leave is four times the weekly working hours. Statutory days expire 6 months after the year ends, extra-statutory days after 5 years. Holiday allowance (vakantiebijslag) is at least 8% of the gross salary.

label: 30% ruling (Netherlands)
answer: The ruling is being phased down, so check the start date of the employee. It requires recruitment from abroad, a minimum salary and distance to the Dutch border. The application has to go to the tax authority within 4 months of starting.

label: UK payroll (PAYE)
answer: UK payroll runs on PAYE with Real Time Information: every pay run is reported to HMRC on or before payday. New starters without a P45 fill in a starter checklist so the right tax code can be applied.

label: Social elections & works council
answer: Candidates are protected against dismissal from the moment the procedure starts. Social elections run every 4 years, the next ones in 2028, and the procedure starts 150 days before the election day.

label: Warrants & stock options
answer: Stock options are taxed when they are granted, on a lump-sum basis, if accepted within 60 days. RSUs are taxed at vesting as salary. Warrants as a bonus are no longer attractive for social security purposes.
